subject: Media Literacy
title: Bias vs. Perspective
description: A 60-second lesson on Bias vs. Perspective.

hook.text: A reporter writes about poverty after growing up poor. Is that bias or valuable perspective? It's complicated.

buildup.text: Perspective is the viewpoint shaped by experience. Bias is when that viewpoint distorts factual reporting.

discovery.text: Perspective can enrich journalism by adding depth. Bias undermines it by sacrificing accuracy for a narrative.

twist.text: The same background can produce either bias or insight depending on whether the journalist acknowledges it.

climax.text: The issue isn't having a perspective. It's pretending you don't have one while it shapes your reporting.

punchline.text: Everyone has a perspective. Bias starts when you deny it.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between bias and perspective?
options: Perspective adds depth while bias distorts factual accuracy
